title: Nature of Matter: Elements, Compounds and Mixtures
seo_title: Nature of Matter Class 8 Science Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8)
standard_code: Class 8, Curiosity Chapter 8: Nature of Matter
standard_text: Pure substances and mixtures; elements, their symbols and atoms; compounds, molecules and formulas; properties of compounds compared with mixtures; homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures; alloys (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 8 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 8: elements and their symbols, compounds and formulas, mixtures, homogeneous and heterogeneous mixtures, and how compounds differ from mixtures. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Elements have one kind of atom; compounds join elements in a fixed ratio.
key_sub: Mixtures keep the properties of their parts.
body_html:
How to think about it

An element is made of only one kind of atom and is shown by a symbol, such as O for oxygen and Fe for iron. A compound is made of two or more elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio, such as water (H₂O) and carbon dioxide (CO₂); it has new properties and can be broken down only by chemical methods.

A mixture contains substances mixed in any proportion without a chemical change, so its parts keep their properties and can be separated by physical methods. Mixtures are homogeneous (the same throughout, like salt water) or heterogeneous (like sand and water). Alloys such as brass and steel are mixtures.

Example

Symbol of copper?

from the Latin 'cuprum'

Answer: Cu

Example

Iron and sulphur, not heated: element, compound or mixture?

a magnet can remove the iron

Answer: a mixture

Common mistakes

  • Calling air a compound.
  • Calling brass an element.
  • Thinking a compound keeps the properties of its elements.

faq.q: What is the difference between a compound and a mixture?
faq.a: A compound has elements chemically joined in a fixed ratio with new properties; a mixture has parts that are not chemically joined and keep their own properties.

faq.q: Why is the symbol of iron Fe?
faq.a: It comes from 'ferrum', the Latin name for iron.
